subject: Priority: Dedicated GPU pool saturation & reserved throughput shortfall
messages:
From: Alice Nguyen <alice@primebank.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 07:45:12 -0800
Subject: High error rates and 5xx during morning window — Prod impact

Rachel —

We're seeing a sustained spike across our inference endpoints this morning during the 07:15-07:40 PST window. Quick metrics from our side:
- 95th percentile latency jumped from ~450ms to ~1.8s
- 5xx error rate climbed to ~5% (baseline ~0.2%)
- Reserved throughput for our tier shows an effective shortfall of ~30% compared to committed QPS

This is impacting several customer-facing flows (KYC validation and fraud checks). We're attaching the request traces and representative error payloads (error_samples.zip) — you can see repeated queueing and token-timeouts. Can you confirm this is related to a dedicated GPU pool saturation on your side and, if so, what immediate mitigations you can deploy? We need:
- ETA for a mitigation that restores 95th below 700ms
- Whether you can temporarily route our traffic to a higher-capacity pool or enable an emergency burst
- Any short-term client-side workarounds we should apply (throttling guidance)

Ops are watching; looping in David since they've worked this account. Please advise asap.

Thanks,
Alice Nguyen
Head of Platform Engineering | PrimeBank
alice@primebank.com

Attachments: error_samples.zip, initial_request_traces.json
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 08:02:47 -08:00
Subject: Re: High error rates and 5xx during morning window — Prod impact

Team — escalating to ops + exec: PrimeBank reports a significant latency and 5xx spike coincident with high token-rate bursts. Summary from their telemetry: 95th ~1.8s, error rate ~5%, reserved throughput shortfall ~30%. They attached traces.

Immediate asks (we need fast decisions):
- Can infra allocate a short-term add-on to PrimeBank's dedicated pool (hot spare / emergency GPUs) for the next 4 hours?
- Ops: run the dedicated-pool-shedding playbook (INF-4921) to free headroom and enable tenant-based per-route rate limiting.
- Finance/Sales (Marissa): can you pre-approve a small customer credit and sign off on a rapid procurement path if we need to keep extra capacity for >24h?
- Exec bridge: propose 11:00 PST with PrimeBank CTO and our CTO (Vivek) if we can't get latency under control by 10:30.

Proposed short-term mitigations (suggested by SRE):
1) Temporarily lower concurrency for non-critical PrimeBank routes (10-15% throttling)
2) Reduce model-context length for risky endpoints (config change rolling to canary)
3) Spin up 2 GPUs in the hot spare pool mapped to PrimeBank routing tag
4) Enable emergency KV-prefix caching for their top 3 request patterns

I'm on standby to join the customer bridge. David — can you pull the 15m headroom chart and estimate ETA to get 95th < 700ms if we apply the above? Attaching the quick SLO snapshot we pulled (slo_95th_latency_chart.png).

-Rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 09:14:33 -08:00
Subject: Re: Priority: Dedicated GPU pool saturation & reserved throughput shortfall

Rachel / team — thanks for the quick triage. Ops can start the shedding and canary config immediately; SRE estimates 18-35 minutes to enact and observe impact. Action items I can own now:
- I'll draft a customer-facing note that contains the mitigation plan, expected timelines, and an offer of a credit if SLA thresholds are not met. Recommend a 15% credit applied to Dec invoice as immediate good-faith (subject to legal/finance sign-off).
- I'll open a procurement ticket to reserve extra capacity if the shortfall persists beyond the initial 2-hour window — procurement path will take ~3-6 hours for hot-spare allocation, but we can confirm availability sooner.
- Vivek: need your blessing on potential emergency reallocation of 4 GPUs from the generic hotspare pool to PrimeBank routing tag for the next 12 hours. This will increase cost exposure; I'll prepare an offsetting credit plan and an authorization request.

David — can you confirm whether this shortfall looks like noisy-neighbor (tenant-level burst) vs kernel-level regression? If noisy-neighbor we follow tenant rate-limits + temporary reallocation. If kernel regression we may need to fall back to a slightly older quantized model for PrimeBank while kernels are verified.

I'll stand by for the exec bridge and will sync the briefing note (customer_maup_plan.docx) in 30m.

-Marissa
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@primebank.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 12:06:01 -08:00
Subject: Re: High error rates and 5xx during morning window — Prod impact

Alice — thank you for the quick signal and the traces. We're actively executing a mitigation plan and wanted to summarize next steps and timelines:

What we did (in the last 60 minutes):
- SRE enacted tenant-level shedding for PrimeBank non-critical routes (10% concurrency reduction).
- Deployed a canary config that reduces max model context for the three highest-volume endpoints.
- Spun up two GPUs from hot spare and mapped them to your routing tag; this added ~18% headroom immediately.

Observed impact (preliminary):
- 95th latency reduced from 1.8s to ~820ms in the canary cohort
- 5xx rate dropping but still above baseline (~1.2% now)

Next steps (if we do not hit target by 10:30 PST):
- Allocate up to 4 additional GPUs from hot spares for up to 12 hours. Vivek is evaluating this now.
- If needed, we will temporarily route a fraction of traffic to a higher-capacity pool under an emergency routing policy.
- We will offer a good-faith credit (Marissa is aligning finance/legal) — provisional plan: 15% credit for any SLA shortfall during this event; final number to be agreed in the 11:00 exec bridge.

Request: please share any correlation IDs you see for failed requests so we can prioritize those traces (David is triaging). We have a 11:00 PST bridge scheduled to confirm next steps; invite link: https://meet.google.com/xyz-primemeeting

Apologies for the disruption — we're prioritizing restoration and will follow up with the post-incident writeup (root cause and long-term prevention) within 24 hours.

Regards,
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwood.com

Attachments: slo_95th_latency_chart.png, billing-impact.csv, customer_maup_plan.docx
